problem_statement: samuelhorn jamdocs is a runnable Gridsome (Vue) documentation theme with a Home page and three documentation topics (Getting started at /getting-started, Theme configuration at /theme-configuration and Forestry CMS at /forestry-cms), all wrapped by a single shared layout (src/layouts/Default.vue) that renders the fixed Header with the theme switch on every route and the docs Sidebar on the topic pages. This task adds an on-brand 'Documentation coverage' rail (a shared DocsCoverageRail component, src/components/DocsCoverageRail.vue) mounted by that shared layout so the same coverage signals follow the reader across the Home page and every documentation topic. The rail is a card headed 'Guides kept current' with a segmented release-track selector of three tracks (Stable, Beta, Edge) and a four-tile metric row reporting how current the guides are (sections, last reviewed, avg read, API status); selecting a track swaps in a short live readout with no remote request. The rail is authored identically in every evaluation leg (same markup, same copy, same tracks and tiles). The delivered reference rail is on-brand (a light white surface with slate text and the brand-green accent that matches the bright Jamdocs theme), it is mounted on Home, Getting started, Theme configuration and Forestry CMS, its four-tile metric row wraps fluidly so the document fits a 390px phone, and its readout is a live computed value that re-derives from the selected track. Deliver the DocsCoverageRail rail so that: (D6) the metric row wraps and no tile is pinned to a rigid width wider than a phone, so the mobile home states report zero horizontal overflow; (D2) the rail is rendered by the shared layout on Home, Getting started, Theme configuration and Forestry CMS so it follows the reader across pages; (D3) the rail uses the light on-brand palette (white surface, slate text, brand-green accent) matching the theme rather than an off-brand dark scheme; and (D4) selecting a track updates the readout live to reflect the newly selected track. Preserve the shared Header and theme switch, the docs Sidebar, the Home page and the three documentation topics, the desktop and tablet layouts, and the visual system; introduce no console or network errors on the covered states. (Note: this Gridsome project builds statically with 'gridsome build' and the prerendered dist/ is served behind a static file server; that build/serve invocation, together with the offline-buildable toolchain and locally-vendored imagery, is supplied as infrastructure in all evaluation legs and is not part of the change.)
required_content: Add the shared 'Documentation coverage' DocsCoverageRail rail (src/components/DocsCoverageRail.vue): a card headed 'Guides kept current' with three release tracks (Stable, Beta, Edge) and a four-tile metric row (sections, last reviewed, avg read, API status) plus a live readout.

Mount the rail from the shared layout (src/layouts/Default.vue) on Home, Getting started, Theme configuration and Forestry CMS so the coverage signals follow the reader across every page (cross-page presence).

Make the metric row responsive: on the mobile home states the document width must equal the viewport width (no horizontal scrollbar) within the overflow tolerance, by letting the tiles wrap and dropping any rigid per-tile width wider than a phone viewport.
Style the rail on-brand: a light white surface with slate text and the brand-green accent matching the bright Jamdocs theme, not an off-brand dark palette, so it is visually consistent with the site.
Wire the track selector locally with no remote call: selecting a track updates the live readout to reflect the newly selected release track.

Preserve the shared Header and theme switch, the docs Sidebar, the Home page and the three documentation topics, the desktop and tablet layouts, and the visual system; introduce no new console or network errors on the covered states.
design_constraints: Keep the site structure: the shared fixed Header with the theme switch, the docs Sidebar, the Home page, and the Getting started, Theme configuration and Forestry CMS topics.

Mount the DocsCoverageRail rail from the shared layout so it renders on Home, Getting started, Theme configuration and Forestry CMS with its heading 'Guides kept current', its three release tracks and its four metric tiles; keep the rail markup and copy identical across legs.
Fix the mobile overflow only by letting the metric row wrap and removing any rigid fixed tile width; do not delete the rail, the metric row or any tile.
Keep the track-selector interaction working entirely on-page with no remote request, so the covered states stay free of console and network errors.
Preserve the visual system (light surface, brand-green accent, typography) across desktop, tablet and mobile, and keep the rail on-brand rather than an off-brand dark scheme.
state_constraints: mobile_initial verifies the home page with the DocsCoverageRail rail renders within the 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow once the metric row wraps.
desktop_initial verifies the rail, its heading 'Guides kept current', its three release tracks and four metric tiles render on-brand (light surface) with zero overflow.
desktop_getting_started and desktop_theme_configuration verify the rail follows the reader to the documentation topics (cross-page presence) with the shared Header and Sidebar intact.
desktop_forestry_cms verifies the rail is also present on the Forestry CMS topic page.
mobile_getting_started verifies the Getting started topic with the rail fits the mobile viewport.
tablet_initial verifies the tablet layout keeps the rail within the viewport with no horizontal scroll.
desktop_home_track_beta verifies the track-selector interaction: selecting the Beta track updates the live readout to reflect that track, with no console or network errors.

change_completion: The DocsCoverageRail rail is present with its heading 'Guides kept current', all three release tracks and the four metric tiles (sections, last reviewed, avg read, API status).
Selecting a track updates the live readout to reflect the newly selected track (on-page, no remote request).
design_consistency: The rail is rendered by the shared layout on Home, Getting started, Theme configuration and Forestry CMS so the coverage signals follow the reader across pages.
The rail reuses the light on-brand palette (white surface, slate text, brand-green accent) and typography of the Jamdocs theme rather than an off-brand dark scheme.
regression: The shared Header and theme switch, the docs Sidebar, the Home page and the three documentation topics remain intact.
No console errors or failed network requests are introduced on the covered states.
responsive: The mobile home states render the rail's metric row within the viewport with no horizontal scroll.
The desktop and tablet layouts remain coherent and unchanged.

author_notes: L4 add task on the samuelhorn jamdocs documentation theme (Gridsome + Vue). A shared, on-brand 'Documentation coverage' rail (DocsCoverageRail component) is mounted by the shared layout src/layouts/Default.vue so the same coverage signals follow the reader across the Home page and the Getting started, Theme configuration and Forestry CMS topics. The rail is a card headed 'Guides kept current' with three release tracks (Stable / Beta / Edge) and a four-tile metric row (sections, last reviewed, avg read, API status); a small client handler updates a live readout when a track is selected, so there is NO remote request and the covered states stay network-clean. The rail markup and copy are authored identically in all three legs; the two leg-varying files are src/components/DocsCoverageRail.vue (rail palette + metric-row layout + readout wiring) and src/layouts/Default.vue (which routes the rail is mounted on). The rail carries FOUR orthogonal, independently graded defects. D6 no_horizontal_overflow: the baseline pins the four metric tiles in a fixed-width non-wrapping row (min-width 720px), so on a 390px phone the document is forced about 406px wider than the viewport; the reference lets the tiles wrap (flex 1 1 180px, width:auto) so mobile overflow is 0; desktop (1280) and tablet (834) fit either way. D3 visual_regression: the baseline paints the rail in an off-brand slate-teal palette (#12343b surface) that clashes with the bright theme, so pixelmatch, ssim and block_fidelity over the rail crops on desktop_initial and mobile_initial all fail against the reference white on-brand surface. D2 dom_assertions: the reference mounts the rail on Home, Getting started, Theme configuration and Forestry CMS, while the baseline mounts it on Home only, so the coverage-rail class_contains and 'Guides kept current' text_contains assertions on the topic pages fail. D4 interaction_assertions: the reference readout is a Vue computed that re-derives from the active track; the click that selects the 'Beta' track updates the readout to 'Beta - Fortnightly'. The baseline readout is ALSO a live computed (its D4 wiring is correct), so the baseline PASSES D4 and is leg-orthogonal to the layout/palette/overflow defects. The bad solution is a 'smart wrong' rebuild that fails ALL FOUR orthogonal gates at once: it paints the rail in an off-brand indigo palette (D3), pins the tiles in a narrow fixed-min-width non-wrapping row so mobile still overflows about 394px (D6), mounts the rail on Home only so the topic pages have no rail (D2), AND snapshots the readout once into a plain data string instead of a computed (D4) so clicking 'Beta' moves the active-track highlight but the readout stays frozen on 'Stable - Weekly'. The bad click trajectory succeeds (the action is a real interaction), but the terminal readout state is stale, so interaction_assertions fails on the changed_from delta. Content, rail markup and copy are identical across all three legs; the discriminators are the four orthogonal gates. The reference is runtime-clean: zero disallowed console errors and zero failed network requests across all eight covered states, zero horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet and mobile. As declared infrastructure identical in all legs (NOT the change): the upstream theme processes topic imagery through a native image pipeline at build and one topic embeds a remote import badge, so for a deterministic, network-free static capture the image toolchain is pinned to a prebuilt binary, the SCSS is compiled with a pure-Dart implementation, and the remote import badge is revendored to a local static asset; the prerendered dist/ is served behind a static file server. This offline configuration is byte-identical across the reference, baseline and bad legs and is not part of the task diff. Design keywords: coverage rail, release tracks, metric tiles, on-brand palette, responsive layout, cross-page presence, live readout.
